root_policy: Do not change Aza’raan languages or naming

entries.name: Kaluseban
entries.phonetic_design: Korean-inspired consonant economy and rhythmic syllables meet French-style flowing vowels and r/l transitions. Allow occasional nasal final in historical names.
entries.naming_template: Fuse a Korean-inspired meaningful root and French-inspired root. Transform both for the fictional Kaluseban phonology; avoid simply attaching two unchanged real words.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: gyer = constancy; fer = resolution; mer = devoted care; thal = enduring bond (all fictional Kaluseban root interpretations).
entries.custom_notes: User supplied the ten sample fusions. "Han-gyeol" means steady or consistent in the user example and French ferme means firm. The new blends are Kaluseban proposals, not Korean or French words.

entries.name: Tamhiogal
entries.phonetic_design: Arabic-inspired emphatic or pharyngeal-feeling transitions are adapted for fiction; Polish-inspired sibilants, soft consonants and clusters are smoothed for Tamhiogal speech. Never require difficult clusters for every speaker.
entries.naming_template: Meaning root + water or family root; the second root may modify the first. Endings -a, -in and -eya are optional regional inventions.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: nur = light or beacon; fala = returning wave; mir = sheltered reef; zaw = pledge (fictional Tamhiogal root meanings, not claims about Earth translation).
entries.custom_notes: Arabic nūr and Polish fala are real lexical examples meaning light and wave. The blends are inventions, not phrases in either language.

examples.name: Nurfaleya
examples.proposed_meaning: A light returning with the tide

examples.name: Zawadira
examples.proposed_meaning: One who keeps a promise across the sea

entries.name: Dril'thar
entries.syllable_pattern: Optional CLICK + CV.CV or CV.CV.CV; do not require a click in every name
entries.phonetic_design: Egyptian transliteration inspires consonant-rich pictorial ancestry, Navajo inspires controlled vowel length, nasality, tone and selected glottalic contrasts; Taa supplies the click articulation model. No literal Navajo or Taa words are copied.
entries.naming_template: Honor name = optional click onset + one or two fictional roots + community ending. A click may also appear medially; ceremonial and everyday names can differ.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: khe = river memory; sena = refuge; maru = glimmer; naki = ancestral path; tsu = listening (all constructed Dril’thar roots).
entries.custom_notes: All Dril’thar naming traditions belong to Dril’thar communities. Taa click symbols indicate distinct sounds, not decoration. No direct Egyptian-era vowel pronunciation is claimed.

examples.name: Nakiǃra
examples.proposed_meaning: One whose voice returns with the tide

examples.name: Khenáru
examples.proposed_meaning: Glow in the marsh at night

examples.name: ǃTsenamaru
examples.proposed_meaning: Bright memory carried in the current

entries.name: Azrahai
entries.phonetic_design: Georgian-inspired consonant clusters are tempered by Japanese-inspired open, mora-like rhythms.
entries.naming_template: Clan root + chosen element or vocation root; historical lineage titles remain unchanged.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: zari = vow; koro = storm; mera = shelter; tavi = beginning.
entries.custom_notes: Strict JSON establishes the canonical Azrahai name and nine named lineages. Azh’raim is the ancient name of the same people now called Azrahai; its pronunciation and spelling simplified through history.

examples.name: Tavikoro

entries.name: Gandirosha
entries.phonetic_design: Irish-inspired slender versus broad consonant coloring alongside Yoruba-inspired clear vowel sequences and optional melody; no claim that fictional tones carry Yoruba meanings.
entries.naming_template: Personal root + relationship or journey root. The same name may appear in two community pronunciations.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: gora = road; eni = quick wit; sefa = goodwill; muni = fortunate meeting.
entries.custom_notes: Keep dream and mischief lore separate from stereotypes based on source languages.

examples.name: Goraeni
examples.proposed_meaning: A fortunate meeting on the road

examples.name: Enigora
examples.proposed_meaning: One who sees an unexpected route

entries.name: Panolima
entries.phonetic_design: Icelandic-inspired fricative and compound-root density meet Swahili-inspired open final vowels and rhythmic affixation.
entries.naming_template: Given name + optional elemental kin term; elemental affinity must not be inferred from the name.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: svali = stability; nuru = glow; kima = balance; thara = renewal.
entries.custom_notes: All five established elements share one broad naming tradition with voluntary local variations.

entries.name: Gwynis
entries.phonetic_design: Welsh-inspired liquids and initial consonant combinations meet Tamil-inspired long vowel timing, retroflex contrast and rhythmic name endings.
entries.naming_template: Dream image root + memory or witness root.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: gwen = luminous trace; amil = memory; rathi = dream threshold; vena = revelation.
entries.custom_notes: Meanings belong to the fictional Gwynis lexicon, not to the Earth inspirations.

entries.name: Geisamahi
entries.syllable_pattern: CV.CV.CV, vowel harmony preferred within long names
entries.phonetic_design: Finnish-inspired vowel harmony and consonant length combine with Tagalog-inspired repeated syllables or personal relational particles.
entries.naming_template: Place or craft root + playful or affectionate repetition, chosen by the individual.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: sumi = fast path; tala = tool; kani = curiosity; mika = patient work.
entries.custom_notes: Repeat syllables for rhythm without asserting a literal Tagalog translation.

examples.name: Sumitala
examples.proposed_meaning: One who finds the hidden route

entries.name: Jaspey
entries.phonetic_design: Basque-inspired compact stems and consonant alternations pair with Thai-inspired smooth syllable boundaries and distinctive vowel length.
entries.naming_template: Personal root + mushroom or shelter theme only by choice, not enforced by biological form.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: zuri = pale morning; mai = gentle care; keri = shelter; lun = lantern.
entries.custom_notes: Mosscap, Gloomtail and Rotcap are forms, not separate species or mandatory naming castes.

examples.name: Lunkerai
examples.proposed_meaning: A light hidden in the grove

entries.name: Aburata
entries.phonetic_design: Persian-inspired consonant and flowing vowel connections meet Māori-inspired open syllables and steady vowel sequencing.
entries.naming_template: Chosen attribute root + kin or place root; reject automatic evil-coded names.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: rava = warmth; mana = belonging; zeri = perseverance; aro = shared bond.
entries.custom_notes: These are fictional name meanings; do not copy culturally protected names or religious titles.

examples.name: Zerimana
examples.proposed_meaning: One who does not abandon family

entries.name: Deorbasun
entries.phonetic_design: Quechua-inspired syllable shaping meets Turkish-inspired vowel harmony and suffix chains.
entries.naming_template: Soul-animal relationship is optional in a given name. Family, habitat and earned titles may follow the name.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: kira = watchful bond; suni = high path; talka = steadiness; aru = returning kin.
entries.custom_notes: Soul-animal selection remains an open lineage rather than a forced species-specific personality.

examples.name: Arutalka
examples.proposed_meaning: One who returns to the family

entries.name: Volsarii
entries.phonetic_design: Latin-inspired inflectional-looking endings meet Japanese-inspired syllable timing. Fictional morphology must not be passed off as Latin grammar.
entries.naming_template: Given name + service title only when actually held; life-stage titles are not compulsory.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: vita = continuity of life; sora = open sky; mira = crossing; sen = compassionate witness.
entries.custom_notes: The number of lives is undetermined. Wing acquisition in the final life is established.

examples.name: Soramira
examples.proposed_meaning: A passage under the open sky

entries.name: Zirramunis
entries.phonetic_design: Armenian-inspired stop and fricative combinations meet Indonesian-inspired open vowels and transparent compound formation.
entries.naming_template: Apprenticeship or personal value root + craft or place root.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: zir = enduring craft; ruma = household workshop; tan = tempered; sari = shared knowledge.
entries.custom_notes: Source-supported people, but not a named entry in the strict 12-species register; final playable status requires reconciliation.

entries.name: Garuraqets
entries.phonetic_design: Amharic-inspired emphatic-looking consonant contrast pairs with Indonesian-inspired regular vowel grouping and optional reduplication.
entries.naming_template: Nature or feeling root + flight, shelter or friendship root.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: gura = leaflight; qeti = whispered path; mali = bloom; teru = belonging.
entries.custom_notes: Source-supported people, but not a named entry in the strict 12-species register. Do not claim real Amharic etymologies.

examples.name: Qetimali
examples.proposed_meaning: One who notices the hidden bloom

entries.name: Iamhazira
entries.phonetic_design: Punjabi-inspired aspirated and retroflex contrasts meet Nahuatl-inspired lateral /tl/-like sequences and word-shaping affixes.
entries.naming_template: An earned promise root + place, clan or perseverance root.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: iam = strength through practice; haz = vigilance; tlani = oath; vira = resilience.
entries.custom_notes: Source-supported people; strict register inclusion requires author confirmation. Honor and courage are optional themes, not inherent personality traits.

entries.name: Kalus’aan
entries.syllable_pattern: Kaluseban-inspired CV.CV.CV with optional family variant
entries.phonetic_design: Parentage includes Aza’raan and Kaluseban; this is a mixed-ancestry identity, not proof of an independently evolved separate ancestral language.
entries.naming_template: Select any family name tradition. One common option is the Kaluseban fusion; never require a genetic mixing of syllables.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: gyer = constancy; mera = shelter; fani = friendship.
entries.custom_notes: Aza’raan is intentionally NOT given new naming or grammar rules in this pass.

entries.name: Kalusogal
entries.syllable_pattern: CV.CV.CV, softened clusters and long mid vowels
entries.phonetic_design: Parentage includes Tideborn Kaluseban and Tamhiogal. Korean and Arabic supply contrasting inspiration; Polish and French may influence inherited family forms without mandating four-way blends.
entries.naming_template: Tidal family root + chosen individual meaning root. Either parent culture may supply the full name.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: mara = joined tides; nur = guiding light; gyena = lasting union.
entries.custom_notes: Recorded mixed identity; not an additional strict registry species.

entries.name: Aza’zira
entries.phonetic_design: Parentage includes Aza’raan and Iamhazira. Punjabi and Nahuatl remain the specific phonetic inspiration for Iamhazira-side names; no separate Aza’raan rules are rewritten.
entries.naming_template: Personal name may follow Iamhazira tradition, another family tradition or an entirely chosen name.
entries.constructed_semantic_roots: iam = steady practice; tlan = promise; vira = endurance; aza = kinship (fictional name roots).
entries.custom_notes: Documented mixed community, not automatically a distinct species.
